title: : "Coercion — Conditional Documentation ('si no se calma') Threatening Withdrawal of Statutory Notice"

allegation_summary: STG-29 SEG 66–70 (232.78s–253.61s): after promising the document (SEG 41–42), [[SPK-diego-latam-supervisor]] reverses and says 'ni siquiera corresponde que yo le entregue una carta', followed by 'si no se calma, la idea es que nos ayudemos'. Conditioning the delivery of a statutory notice (LPDC Art. 23 bis / CACH Art. 133) on the passenger's demeanour is moral/psychological coercion: it compels the passenger to refrain from exercising the lawful right to protest and to demand documentation. The conduct meets CPCL Art. 494.16 ('impedir a otro con violencia hacer lo que la ley no prohibe') and is reinforced as apremio ilegitimo under CONST Art. 19.1.

articles.article_name: Codigo Penal de Chile, Art. 494 N°16 — Coaccion / Apremio
articles.article_text: El que sin estar legitimamente autorizado impidiere a otro con violencia hacer lo que la ley no prohibe, o le compeliere a ejecutar lo que no quiera.
articles.applicability_rationale: Threatening to withhold a statutory denied-boarding notice unless the passenger 'se calma' compels him to refrain from exercising the lawful right to protest and demand documentation, satisfying Art. 494.16 ('impedir a otro con violencia hacer lo que la ley no prohibe'). The conduct is reinforced as apremio ilegitimo under CONST Art. 19.1. | legacy paraphrase: Sufriran la pena de multa de una a cuatro unidades tributarias mensuales: 16. candidate_articles.candidate_name: Ley del Consumidor, Art. 13 — Constreñimiento al consumidor
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.LPDC.Art.13 from bcn.cl/leychile, focusing on threat-based coercion of consumer acts unrelated to contract formation
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The supervisor's threat to withhold a statutory denied-boarding notice unless the passenger 'se calma' arguably constrains the passenger to refrain from lawful protest—an 'acto' under Art. 13 prohibited if compelled by threats. Verify whether post-sale, non-contractual acts (e.g., ceasing complaints) are covered by the provision's broad wording ('ejecutar cualquier otro acto').
candidate_articles.history_note: Proposed by analyst as a consumer-protection analogue to CPCL 494.16; candidate replaces a previously unverified suggestion from the pipeline.

candidate_articles.candidate_name: Código Civil, Art. 2314 — Responsabilidad extracontractual por delito o cuasidelito civil
verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for CL.CC.Art.2314 from bcn.cl/leychile, confirming it grounds liability for civil wrongs causing damage
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: If the passenger suffered moral or material damage from the coercive threat, Art. 2314 could serve as the primary indemnification hook. The provision's generality makes it almost always a fallback, but care must be taken to link the threat directly to a legally cognizable harm.
candidate_articles.history_note: Added because coercive conduct, if proven harmful, typically gives rise to a civil remedy; this is a standard accompaniment to the criminal-type article already invoked.
